text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Iraqi authorities declare a U.N. guard person non-grata and prevent him from re-entering Iraq; Iraq protests to the United Nations against illegal actions of one of its guards.
- Iraq and Russia discuss U.S. threats.
- Arab countries concerned over curbs on flights by Sudanese civilian aircraft.
- Millions of Turks are victims of U.N. sanctions on Iraq.
- Iraq protests to the United Nations. over violations of its airspace by U.S. and allied aircraft.
- More oil products ferried to Kurdish areas.
- Russia does not recognise no-fly zones.
- Russia exerting efforts for a quick implementation of the oil-for-food deal.
- More countries come out in support of Iraq against U.S. threats to use force against it.
(The above were also carried by QADISSIYA and IRAQ)
- Editorial says Iraq will not accept violations of its sovereignty and its decision to stop firing at U.S. and allied warplanes was for the sake of finding a non-military solution to the conflict.
- Russia and China support proposal to discuss American aggression against Iraq in an international parliamentary conference.
- The paper publishes letter to Bill Clinton from an Iraqi citizen in which the U.S. president is denounced as "barbaric, arrogant and riotous".
- Arab League secretary-general renews support for Iraq in confrontation with American aggression.
